datasets.title: Building Damage Assessment in Paikgachha Upazila, Khulna District, Khulna Division, Bangladesh as of 4 June 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240502BGD, GDACS ID: 1001064 This map illustrates potentially damaged structures as observed by using a Pléiades satellite image acquired on 4 June 2024 at 10:31 Local Time. Within the analysis extent, UNOSAT identified 64 damaged structures and 1,484 potentially damaged structures. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/building-damage-assessment-in-paikgachha-upazila-khulna-district-khulna-division-banglades]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts performed visual interpretation and multi-temporal comparison of Pléiades satellite imagery acquired on 4 June 2024 to detect structural damage in Paikgachha Upazila following a tropical cyclone event. Damaged structures were classified by confidence level and compiled into vector geodatabase and shapefile formats for spatial analysis.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Post-event damage assessment derived from Pléiades satellite imagery acquired on 4 June 2024, identifying 64 confirmed damaged and 1,484 potentially damaged structures through visual interpretation and change detection analysis.
